syllabusTopics: Saturated hydrocarbons (Alkanes): preparation from haloalkanes (reduction and Wurtz reaction), decarboxylation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkene and alkyne
Chemical properties of alkanes: substitution reactions (halogenation, nitration and sulphonation only), oxidation of ethane
Unsaturated hydrocarbons (Alkenes): preparation by dehydration of alcohol, dehydrohalogenation, catalytic hydrogenation of alkyne
Chemical properties of alkenes: addition reaction with HX (Markovnikov's addition and peroxide effect), H2O, O3, H2SO4 only
Alkynes: preparation from carbon and hydrogen, 1,2-dibromoethane, chloroform/iodoform only
Chemical properties of alkynes: addition reaction with H2, HX, H2O; acidic nature (action with sodium, ammoniacal AgNO3 and ammoniacal Cu2Cl2)
Test of unsaturation (ethene and ethyne): bromine water test and Baeyer's test
Comparative studies of physical properties of alkane, alkene and alkyne
Kolbe's electrolysis methods for the preparation of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes

rows.text: Two colour tests expose unsaturation. **Bromine water**: ethene discharges the red-brown instantly — **CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → BrCH₂CH₂Br**; ethyne consumes **two** Br₂ — **CHBr₂CHBr₂**; ethane does nothing **in the dark** (UV would substitute, so darkness keeps the test honest).…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Unsaturated hydrocarbons instantly decolourise bromine water (addition) and cold alkaline KMnO4 (Baeyer's test, brown MnO2); saturated hydrocarbons do neither in the dark."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The negative control*** — ethane's refusal to decolourise bromine water in the dark is as informative as ethene's instant surrender: absence is evidence.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Two Drops That Tell the Truth Unsaturation announces itself in colour: **bromine water** decolourises (addition across π), and **Baeyer's reagent** — cold, dilute, alkaline KMnO₄ — loses its purple and deposits a brown solid (**Baeyer's test**). Ethene and ethyne pass both; ethane fails both.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Bromine water test - **CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ (aq) → BrCH₂CH₂Br** (1,2-dibromoethane) — the **red-brown/orange colour of Br₂ disappears instantly** at room temperature, without catalyst. - Ethyne: **HC≡CH + 2Br₂ → CHBr₂CHBr₂** (1,1,2,2-tetrabromoethane) — colour goes, twice over. - Alkanes: no decolourisation in the dark/cold (substitution needs UV) — the negative control.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Br2 water: alkene 1 eq, alkyne 2 eq, alkane nil (dark). Baeyer: purple → brown MnO2 + diol. Cold + dilute = diol; hot + conc = cleavage. Ethyne vs ethene: ammoniacal AgNO3.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): How will you distinguish ethane, ethene and ethyne using bromine water? (2m)** — Bubble each gas through **bromine water** (red-brown) **in the dark and cold**. **Ethene:** the colour is **instantly discharged** by **addition** across the double bond: **CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → BrCH₂–CH₂Br** (1,2-dibromoethane).…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Describe Baeyer's test for ethene with equation.** — Shake ethene with **cold, dilute, alkaline potassium permanganate** — **Baeyer's reagent**. The **purple permanganate is decolourised** and a **brown precipitate of MnO₂** appears, while the double bond is converted into two hydroxyl groups (**syn dihydroxylation**):…

rows.text: In the NEB 2024 answer, give all three behaviours plus the ethyne-vs-ethene tie-breaker (ammoniacal AgNO3) — that extra sentence secures full marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Two drops, one verdict: bromine tests addition, permanganate tests oxidisability — a π bond fails both; a σ-only skeleton passes both untouched.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Bromine water test: CH2=CH2 + Br2(aq) -> BrCH2CH2Br (instant decolourisation, dark, cold); HCCH + 2Br2 -> CHBr2CHBr2 (tetrabromoethane); ethane no change in dark (UV would substitute - false positive risk).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bromine water was the Victorian chemist's pocket test: a brown loss in one shake meant a double bond long before NMR existed.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Why must the bromine water test be performed away from sunlight?** — Because **ultraviolet light initiates free-radical substitution** of bromine onto **alkanes**: ethane in sunlight would slowly consume Br₂ and fade the colour, producing a **false positive** for unsaturation.…

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the tests work - π electrons are exposed and nucleophilic; Br₂ polarises and adds; KMnO₄ (Mn⁷⁺) is reduced to Mn⁴⁺ (brown MnO₂) while the alkene is oxidised. Saturated σ-frameworks can neither add nor reduce under these mild conditions.…  ·  ## 5. rows.text: State the conditions that keep both tests honest and why.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Dark condition matters for Br₂:** alkanes substitute in UV light — the test is only valid without light.  ·  **Brown ≠ purple:** MnO₂ (brown solid) is the positive sign; faded purple without precipitate is ambiguous — look for the MnO₂.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Both tests say "unsaturated":** neither distinguishes C=C from C≡C alone — pair them with the ammoniacal tests for the full picture.  ·  ## 7.
